transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really hope I'm not wasting your time—I know you probably have patients dealing with much worse things. 

It's just, um... I guess I'm here because I can't quite seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and... well, guilt. I've just been feeling a bit tense most of the day, like I'm constantly waiting for something else to go wrong. And I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. I try not to, but it's just always there in the back of my mind. 

I'm sorry, I'm probably rambling right out of the gate. Is... is this the right kind of thing to come here for?
Can you tell me more about what happened that’s been causing these feelings of fear and guilt?

Well, um... it started about four months ago. We were doing some repairs on our porch at home, and... my husband had a bad fall. He's recovering, thankfully, so I really shouldn't be making a big deal out of it. But ever since it happened, for the last four months, I just haven't been able to shake this feeling. 

I mean, I'm a building inspector, so I just keep thinking I really should have noticed the issue before he stepped on that section, you know? I should have known better and stopped him. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up... I know it's not the worst thing in the world, and he was the one who actually got hurt, not me. Does... does that make sense as to why I'd be feeling this way?
Have you noticed yourself having any recurring, unwanted thoughts or feeling like you need to do certain things over and over again to ease your anxiety?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely think about the fall a lot, but not in a way where I feel like I have to do certain things or... like, repeat actions over and over. I just feel bad about it, that's all. 

I try really hard to just keep busy and not let my mind wander too much. I hope that's the right answer... I don't want to make it sound like I'm doing things that I'm not. Is it normal to just have the thoughts without doing those repetitive things you mentioned?
Have you found yourself having repeated, intrusive thoughts or mental images about the fall that you can’t seem to control?

Um... yeah, I guess I do have those sometimes. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting around obsessing over it, but... I'll just be at work, maybe measuring a railing or... or I'll hear a ladder scrape against a wall, and suddenly it's like... it's like I can see him falling all over again. 

It feels so real, like it's happening right in front of me, and my stomach just drops and my hands get all shaky. I usually just try to take a deep breath and push it away so I can keep working. I really hope that doesn't sound crazy. Is it... is it okay that my mind does that when I hear those noises?
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the fall?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm still working and everything, I'm not totally falling apart. But... I have started, you know, asking my supervisor to give me different assignments if a job involves raised porches or, like, second-story decks. I just... I tell them I'm better suited for ground-level stuff right now. 

And at home... I guess I do kind of find excuses to leave the room if my husband brings up finishing the repairs. I just don't really want to talk about it, or even look at that side of the house where he fell. I know it's probably silly, and I should just get over it. It's just easier to focus on other things right now. I hope it's okay that I'm doing that... is it bad to just want to avoid those things for a little while?
Have you noticed that your feelings of guilt or fear related to the fall have remained consistent over time, or do they come and go?

Well, um... I guess they don't really go away. I mean, I try to stay positive, I really do. I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around complaining all the time. But... yeah, it's just this heavy feeling that I can't seem to shake. 

It's like this mix of being scared and feeling so, so guilty. I'm just kind of tense all day, like I'm waiting for something else terrible to happen, and I just keep blaming myself for not stopping the fall in the first place. I know I should probably be handling it better by now... I really hope it's not abnormal to still feel this way after everything. Is it okay that I'm still struggling with these feelings?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like you're not good enough or worthy of the life you have?

Well, um... I definitely don't want to sound like I'm ungrateful for my life or anything, because I'm really not. I'm still doing okay overall. But... I guess maybe I have been feeling a little down on myself lately. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but... well, because of what I do for a living as an inspector, I just keep thinking that if I missed something so important at my own house, then maybe... maybe I'm just not as careful or competent as I always thought I was. I mean, my work reports are completely fine, they really are! They don't show any mistakes or anything like that, and I'm trying really hard to keep it that way. But I just have this nagging thought in the back of my head that I'm not good enough at what I do anymore. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, especially since my work is still good. Does that... I mean, does that make sense? Is it normal to second-guess yourself like that?
